name: Dull Teal
lede: Dull Teal is a greyed, muted [[teal]], recorded in both Wikipedia's color list and the 2010 xkcd survey.

sections.title: Teal with the shine taken off
sections.body: Our data traces this name to Wikipedia's color list and separately to the 2010 xkcd crowd survey [1]. In the ISCC-NBS 1955 system it falls nearest the block called "light bluish green", 5.4 units off [2]. In Munsell terms it reads about 1.7BG 6.0/4.3, a mid-light, moderately desaturated blue-green [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[montpellier-green]], [[greyish-teal]] and [[venet]], at 3.1, 3.3 and 3.8 ΔE [2]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary separately lists a color called Cabaret at this same point, first recorded in 1925, on plate 27 I 6 [3]. The word "dull" marks the color as teal with its saturation turned down, [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 31 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed [4]. The earliest dated match is Bernardino Jacobi Butinone's *The Descent from the Cross*, from about 1480, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. Its clearest peak is the 1900s, at more than seven times the archive's overall rate [4]. [[painter:henri-matisse|Henri Matisse]] used it far more than most painters, including in his 1905 *[[painting:smk-KMSr171|Portrait of Madame Matisse, The Green Line]]* [4]. Unlike most colors in our archive, it plays a highlight more often than a mid-tone, over half the time, rather than sitting in a painting's shadows [4]. These counts are computed color matches on photographs of aged, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [4].
